chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Imran ibn Musa and Ali ibn Khalid from Harun from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from Abdillah ibn Junadab from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'An elderly man who is unable to fast,' he said: 'Some of his children should fast on his behalf.' I said: 'If he has no children?' He said: 'Then the nearest of his relatives.' I said: 'If he has no relatives?' He said: 'He should give charity with a mud of food for each day. If he has nothing, then there is no obligation upon him.'

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ: Then there is no obligation upon him
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A mud (a traditional unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly person who cannot fast due to old age or chronic illness?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the graduated hierarchy of *fidyah* (expiation) for the permanently incapacitated, prioritizing the eldest son before extending to other kin, a structure reflecting Shia juristic emphasis on familial responsibility. The final provision of feeding a *mudd* (approx. 750g) per day aligns with the Quranic standard for feeding the poor, while the exemption for the destitute underscores the principle of *la haraj* (no hardship) in Islamic law.
